label: ask:Cabin: 21.0% O2 at 4.5 psi, material fabric, airflow ventilated (≈20 cm/s), grav

output.text:
The retrieved records do not directly cover fabric at 21.0% O₂ and 4.5 psi in microgravity. A reduced-pressure microgravity fabric investigation near those conditions, with airflow around 20 cm/s, would address the main gap.

Most relevant, in priority order:

- **Saffire IV–VI:** Most relevant to the pressure gap. Its recorded conditions span 7.85–14.5 psi and 22–31% O₂ at 20 cm/s, but do not reach your cabin pressure. These are hand-transcribed published results, not PSI-archive runs [saffire-iv-vi]. The cotton-jersey example burned at 26.2% O₂ and 10.25 psi; “burned” is a source-field outcome [saffire-v-2].
- **Saffire-I:** Strong fabric-and-airflow match: SIBAL fabric at 20 cm/s and 14.5 psi. One run records 21.6% O₂, the midpoint of a reported range, and a source-field “burned” outcome. Pressure is substantially above your cabin’s [saffire-i-s1].
- **BASS:** Useful complementary coverage of solid-fuel burning and suppression in microgravity, including fabrics. Recorded O₂ spans 15.9–22.72%, but pressure remains 14.26–14.82 psi; airflow and outcomes are missing for some runs [bass].

These experiments support engineering judgment, not predictions at 4.5 psi or replacement of certified material testing.
